title: HTTP transfer adapter on Apache HttpClient 5: blocking, streaming, governed pinning
requirement: ADR-0012 decisions RT-Q5 (Apache HttpClient 5) and RT-Q1; plan §20 RT-03; closes ARCH-09 / DR-X05 (whole-body buffering)
acceptance: Governed HTTPS connects only to the agent-approved address while SNI, Host and hostname verification use the service hostname
A certificate for another name, a leaf-pin mismatch, an unapproved CA and a TLS version below the credential minimum are each rejected for that reason, and nothing is written
Governed transfers never follow redirects; ungoverned transfers do
Bearer and Basic authorization headers are sent from the credential
Downloads stream to <destination>.tmp and appear at the destination only when complete; non-success status and checksum mismatch fail without writing
Uploads stream the file with PUT
The adapter needs no Vert.x instance
classification: external-path behavioural (real JDK HTTP and HTTPS servers, real TLS; no mocks)
fixtures: quorus-core/src/test/resources/security/governed (test CA, leaves for transfer.quorus.test and other.quorus.test, unapproved CA; regeneration commands in its README)
decisionEvidence: JDK 27 java.net.http probe (2026-09-26): a pinned-IP connection with SNI=wrong.test completed the handshake, so the hostname was not enforced against the intended name; Host was the IP and cannot be set (restricted header). Recorded in ADR-0012 RT-Q5.

discardedAttempts.reason: Compile errors in the new test, and an ambiguous constructor call in an existing test (fixture defects)

Five rejection tests passed against the skeleton for the wrong reason, because they only asserted that some TransferException was thrown. They were tightened to assert the specific cause before the red was accepted

The streaming test used WatchService, which on Windows did not report the growing .tmp file. The test hung, and its held server thread kept the test JVM alive. It was redesigned to signal from the transfer thread through a purpose-built TransferContext, with a bounded server wait. The hung test JVM was stopped by specific PID
Test defect in the new aMatchingExpectedChecksumIsAccepted: ChecksumCalculator.getChecksum() finalises the digest and was called twice. The adapter behaved correctly

red.revision: 5a4274f plus skeleton constructors (no client; transfer() still disabled) and the boundary tests
red.result: 13 of 13 failed for the intended reasons: positive paths errored on the skeleton's 'disabled' TransferException; every rejection test failed its cause-specific assertion; the streaming test failed at once

green.change: HttpTransferProtocol rewritten on Apache HttpClient 5 classic: a client per transfer; a governed approved-address DnsResolver; TlsPeerPolicy.governedTrustManager(baseTrust, caIds, pins); HostnameVerificationPolicy.BOTH; the credential's TLS versions; redirects disabled when governed; a streaming GET to .tmp with an incremental checksum, progress and cancellation checks; a streaming PUT; abort() closes in-flight clients. Existing HTTP tests were migrated from transferReactive/Vert.x to the blocking API, and tests of the removed Vertx constructor deleted; ProtocolFactory uses the no-argument constructor

mutationCheck.description: The adapter was temporarily changed to buffer the whole response (the ARCH-09 behaviour); the streaming test failed with 'the transfer ended before writing half a megabyte'; the adapter was restored

refactor: Removed unreachable null checks in validateRequest and canHandle, which TransferRequest's builder already guarantees (non-null URIs; no remote-to-remote requests); extracted the resolver as ApprovedAddressResolver for direct testing

processDeviation.description: Behaviour implemented during green without a preceding failing test is covered by 12 tests classified as retrospective characterization (HttpTransferProtocolBoundaryTest$Characterization): abort, context cancellation, thread interruption, an unpinned governed transfer, a chunked response, a zero-byte file, PASSWORD Basic auth, no header for non-HTTP credential types, an uncreatable destination directory, an empty expected checksum, a matching expected checksum, and the resolver unit behaviour

regression.result: 1,574 tests, 0 failures (before the checksum-match test); JaCoCo gate met

BUILD SUCCESS; 2,443 tests (core 1,575, workflow 134, tenant 64, controller 569, agent 101), 0 failures, all five JaCoCo gates met. HttpTransferProtocol 207/215 lines and 59/60 branches; ApprovedAddressResolver 11/11 lines and 4/4 branches

uncoveredByDesign: entity == null guard: HttpClient 5 supplies an entity for every 200 GET response, including empty bodies (see the zero-byte test)
failure to delete a partial file
limitations: The log of the first full reactor verify after green (16:13-16:18, BUILD SUCCESS, 2,431 tests) was overwritten by the next run; the retained logs are the failed attempt and the final successful run.
Docker and slow groups were not rerun: the controller image does not use the HTTP transfer path, and the agent has no Docker lane.
Governed TLS still validates against the JVM default trust store in production; configurable trust anchors are register item SEC-07.
SimpleTransferEngine still calls transferReactive; the TransferProtocol default hands the blocking transfer() to a Vert.x worker until RT-03c and RT-03d.
sensitiveDataCheck: Logs contain Maven, server and test output only; the bearer and basic secrets are synthetic fixture values.
